Remark. Bose--Einstein condensate vortex data and q-deformed predictions

Bose--Einstein condensates (BECs) provide the cleanest experimental realisation of quantised vortex dynamics [fetter2009, navon2021]. The results below demonstrate that the q \to 1 limit of the \mathrm{SU}_q(2) vortex spectrum (Proposition) correctly reproduces observed BEC phenomenology.

1. Quantised circulation. In {}^{87}\mathrm{Rb} and {}^{23}\mathrm{Na} BECs, vortex circulation is measured to be \Gamma_n = n \cdot h/m, with n an integer [madison2000]. No intermediate values have ever been observed. In the QOU framework, this is the q \to 1 limit of the \mathrm{SU}_q(2) Casimir quantisation. The spin label j reduces to the winding number n, and [j]_q[j+1]_q \to j(j+1) = n(n+1) gives the discrete circulation levels. The BEC data confirms the selection rule |\Delta n| = 1 predicted by the ladder-mode transition mechanism.

2. Vortex lattice formation. Above a critical rotation frequency \Omega_c, BECs nucleate regular lattices of singly-quantised vortices [abo-shaeer2001]. The number of vortices follows the Feynman rule N_v = m \Omega A / (\pi\hbar), where A is the condensate area. This is consistent with the q \to 1 limit of the q-Feynman rule, in which the vortex count is controlled by \hbar_q.

3. Kelvin-mode excitations. Bretin et al. [bretin2003] observed quadrupole oscillations of a single vortex in a {}^{87}\mathrm{Rb} condensate, identified as the lowest Kelvin mode (k = 1). The measured frequency \omega_1^{\text{exp}} = 2\pi \times (6.2 \pm 0.1) Hz matches the Kelvin dispersion relation. The q-deformed prediction replaces k^2 with [k]_q^2 = [1]_q^2 = 1 + O((q-1)^2). This is indistinguishable from the classical value at laboratory q.

4. Vortex clustering and turbulence. Gauthier et al. [gauthier2019] observed giant vortex clusters in 2D {}^{87}\mathrm{Rb} condensates, where same-sign vortices aggregate into macroscopic circulation structures. The cluster circulation is quantised in multiples of the single-vortex quantum. This directly demonstrates the additive structure j_{\text{cluster}} = j_1 + j_2 + \cdots. In the q-deformed framework, cluster formation corresponds to the tensor product of \mathrm{SU}_q(2) representations. The total spin j_{\text{total}} follows the Clebsch--Gordan decomposition of \mathrm{SU}_q(2).

Summary of observed results.

Observable Measured value q \to 1 limit
Circulation quantum \Gamma_n = nh/m, integer n only [j]_q[j+1]_q \to j(j+1)
Vortex lattice count Feynman rule N_v N_v^{(q)} \to N_v
Kelvin k=1 frequency 2\pi \times 6.2 Hz [1]_q^2 \to 1
Cluster circulation integer multiples of h/m \mathrm{SU}_q(2) \to \mathrm{SU}(2) Clebsch--Gordan
